title: Thunderstorms Shoot Antimatter Into Space, NASA Found

scenes.text: Thunderstorms shoot beams of antimatter into space.
In 2011, NASA's Fermi telescope caught it happening.
Inside a storm, lightning creates bursts of gamma rays.
Some of that energy turns into electrons and their antimatter twins.
About 500 of these flashes happen worldwide every day, mostly unseen.
One beam travelled 2,800 miles along Earth's magnetic field.

description:
NASA's Fermi telescope found that thunderstorms hurl beams of antimatter into space.
About 500 gamma-ray flashes happen every day worldwide, mostly unseen.
Did you know storms could do that?
first_comment: A thunderstorm makes antimatter. What other weather secret should we cover?
